Article Title: NEET-UG leak probe: CBI gets 3 more days to file annexures in chargesheet, hearing on August 3
Article Text: NEW DELHI: A special fast-track court at Rouse Avenue on Wednesday listed the CBI's chargesheet in the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak case for consideration on August 3 and granted the agency three more days to file the remaining annexures.The court was informed that the CBI had filed a chargesheet running into around 20,000 pages against 13 accused. The agency sought additional time to file the annexures, witness statements and the list of documents, saying the records were being scanned before being supplied to the accused, according to ANI.Special fast track court Judge Anu Grover Baliga allowed the request and granted the CBI three days to complete the filing.During the hearing, the court noted that the chargesheet submitted on Tuesday was not accompanied by witness statements or the list of documents. The CBI told the court that the records were voluminous and would be filed within three days.Deputy Legal Advisor A P Singh, Senior Public Prosecutor V K Pathak and Public Prosecutor Arjun Anand appeared for the CBI during the hearing.Earlier on Tuesday, the CBI filed a chargesheet against 13 accused, including three National Testing Agency (NTA) subject experts, two coaching centre associates, middlemen and several beneficiary candidates.The agency invoked charges of criminal conspiracy, cheating, criminal breach of trust and destruction of evidence under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), along with offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act and the Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024."The CBI cited 360 witnesses, 422 documents and 43 material objects in this charge sheet. All 13 chargesheeted persons are in judicial custody as on date," the agency's spokesperson had said.The CBI said it had attached digital forensic analysis reports, handwriting expert opinions and academic experts' assessments of the leaked question paper."These reports confirmed the role of the accused in circulation of leaked questions prior to the date of examination," the spokesperson said.The agency took over the probe on May 12 after the Department of Higher Education lodged a complaint over alleged irregularities and a paper leak in the NEET-UG 2026 examination held on May 3. The examination was later cancelled and a re-examination was conducted on June 21.According to the CBI, its two-month investigation traced the alleged conspiracy from the source of the paper leak to the beneficiary candidates, identifying the entire chain involved. The agency also said it had tracked the money trail and frozen several bank accounts, bank lockers and a demat account linked to the accused.Among those named in the chargesheet are three arrested NTA subject experts, PV Kulkarni (Chemistry), Manisha Gurunath Mandhare (Biology) and Manisha Sanjay Havaldar (Physics).Also named are Latur-based doctor Manoj Shirure, Tejas Harshadkumar Shah, a physics faculty member at Pune-based Dr Abhang Prabhu Medical Academy (APMA), and Shivraj Raghunath Motegaonkar of a coaching centre in Latur.
Article Summary: The court was informed that the cbi had filed a chargesheet running into around 20,000 pages against 13 accused. The agency sought additional time to file the annexures, witness statements and the list of documents. Judge anu grover baliga allowed the request and granted the cbi three days to complete the filing.

Article Title: NEET has flaw in design, it is not necessary: DMK's Dayanidhi Maran
Article Text:
File photo: DMK MP Dayanidhi Maran

NEW DELHI: DMK Tuesday demanded that NEET be scrapped as its MP Dayanidhi Maran in Lok Sabha asserted that the proposed amendment in the law against paper leak accused does not address the core problem bedeviling the medical entrance examination."You are not addressing the core issue. NEET is not necessary. DMK and Tamil Nadu were the first to voice their opposition to NEET due to the fundamental flaws in its design. Our warnings were never heard," he said, reiterating his party's stand against the national exam, which replaced state-level entrance tests.No longer part of the opposition INDIA bloc, Maran focused largely on his party's stand against NEET, the entrance exam to medical colleges, while tangentially referring to the recent student protest, the focus of BJP's opponents. Students have compelled parliamentarians to debate NEET, he saidHe alleged that Meta smart glasses had been used to record protesting students, following which police reached their homes. BJP grew on the back of protests, he said, asking the party as to why it was "opposed" to them.BJP is keen on getting support from DMK to push a constitution amend bill rolling out women's reservation from 2029 and raise the number of seats in Lok Sabha by over 50%.Maran claimed he and NCP - SP MP Supriya Sule were unable to use WhatsApp broadcasts for three days because of forwarding limits. "Today by mistake a Facebook post by the PM was removed, and the government called Meta chief to explain. But this is happening to MPs," Maran claimed.
Article Summary: Dmk demands that neet be scrapped as its mp dayanidhi maran in lok sabha. Maran says proposed amendment in law against paper leak accused does not address core problem. Dmk and tamil nadu were the first to voice their opposition to neet due to the fundamental flaws in its design.

Article Title: Union minister, BJP MP got NHB subsidies, mantri refunded it: Government
Article Text:
Union minister Bhagirath Choudhary & BJP MP Lumba Ram

NEW DELHI: Union minister of state for agriculture Bhagirath Choudhary and BJP MP from Sirohi in Rajasthan Lumba Ram received financial assistance under a central scheme in 2026 and 2025, govt informed Parliament Tuesday, adding that Choudhary, however, refunded the subsidy.In a written reply to Lok Sabha, minister of state for agriculture Ramnath Thakur said, "Bhagirath Choudhary has communicated that he has refunded the subsidy to the bank concerned under the scheme. The bank concerned has been directed to return the subsidy amount to the National Horticulture Board (NHB)".He added, "The existing NHB scheme guidelines do not contain any specific provision regarding conflict of interest or recusal in respect of applications submitted by public functionaries or their family members." Thakur was replying to a query by Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee, who wanted to know whether any serving Union minister, MP or their immediate family members received subsidy under schemes of the NHB during the last five years.Thakur said, "The NHB processes all applications for financial assistance under its schemes through a transparent mechanism... All eligible applicants are treated equally, and applications are considered solely on the basis of the eligibility criteria and compliance with the provisions of the scheme."
Article Summary: Bhagirath choudhary and bjp mp from sirohi in rajasthan lumba ram received financial assistance under a central scheme in 2026 and 2025, govt informed parliament tuesday. The minister of state for agriculture refunded the subsidy to the bank concerned under the scheme.

Article Title: Dealers can't keep over 400 tonne stock of sugar: Government
Article Text:
Govt imposes sugar stock holding limits

NEW DELHI: Government on Tuesday issued an order capping the stock of sugar at 400 tonne with any dealer at any point of time till November 30 and traders have been directed to liquidate excess stock by August 1.The directive, which will come into force from August 1, also says that the dealers need to sell the sweetener within 30 days from the date of receipt. Food ministry, which invoked the Essential Commodities Act to issue a gazette notification imposing restriction, said this is being done to prevent hoarding, protect consumer interests, maintain price stability and ensure a transparent and efficient sugar supply chain."Government has observed that the recent increase in ex-mill prices of sugar is not supported by the prevailing demand-supply fundamentals...hoarding by certain traders, dealers and market intermediaries, along with speculative transactions and paper trade without the actual physical movement of sugar from mills, has contributed to creating an artificial perception of scarcity.." the ministry said.To keep prices under check amid a forecast of a deficit monsoon, the Centre has banned sugar exports.The order would not apply to sugar stocks held on govt account, or by dealers nominated by the state government.
Article Summary: Government issues an order capping the stock of sugar at 400 tonne with any dealer at any point of time till november 30. Traders have been directed to liquidate excess stock by august 1. To keep prices under check amid a forecast of a deficit monsoon, the centre has banned sugar exports.

Article Title: Red alert issued in Delhi as heavy rain lashes NCR, waterlogging in several areas
Article Text:
Waterlogging reported in several parts of Delhi-NCR





NEW DELHI: Delhi-NCR woke up to heavy rain on Tuesday, bringing some relief from the humid weather but also triggering waterlogging and traffic snarls at several locations.The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red alert for Delhi, forecasting moderate rain at many places and heavy rain at isolated locations, along with moderate thunderstorms and lightning till 3pm.A traffic snarl was reported on NH-8 in the Shankar Vihar area, while waterlogging was reported at Pandav Nagar Underpass and R/A Murga Mandi, where dewatering is in progress.Traffic personnel have been deployed at the affected locations, and commuters have been advised to drive cautiously and follow their directions.The IMD has forecast moderate rainfall over Delhi on Wednesday, with light to moderate rain likely at several places during the day.According to the IMD's daily weather report issued on Monday, the national capital is likely to witness light rain and thunderstorms over the next few days, with generally cloudy skies and moderate rain at isolated places.Delhi recorded a maximum temperature of 38.1 degrees Celsius and a minimum temperature of 28.6 degrees Celsius at Safdarjung.The IMD said maximum temperatures are likely to fall by 2-3 degrees Celsius over the next six days.According to the IMD, the deep depression was located near the West Bengal coast and was likely to move nearly west-northwestwards and cross the West Bengal-North Odisha coasts near Digha and west of Haldia by early Tuesday morning.The weather system was located close to Digha in West Bengal, with its movement likely to bring rain to several parts of the region.The IMD has advised commuters to check traffic conditions before leaving and avoid areas prone to waterlogging.(With ANI inputs)
Article Summary: Waterlogging reported in several parts of delhi-ncr. Imd has issued a red alert for delhi, forecasting moderate rain at many places. Traffic snarl was reported on nh-8 in shankar vihar area, while waterlogging was reported at pandav nagar underpass.

Article Title: '51 wounds, cold-blooded murder': Prosecution seeks death penalty for ex-AAP neta Tahir Hussain, 4 others in IB officer's murder
Article Text:
IB staffer murder case: Prosecution seeks death sentence for Tahir Hussain, other convicts





New Delhi: The prosecution Monday sought death penalty against former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain and four others convicted of the murder of Intelligence Bureau officer Ankit Sharma during the 2020 northeast Delhi riots.The court of additional sessions judge Parveen Singh was hearing the matter concerning Hussain, Nazim, Kasim, Javed and Anas, who were convicted on July 13.Special public prosecutor Madhukar Pandey argued in the court that the murder was "exceptionally brutal"."Ankit Sharma was abducted and relentlessly assaulted before he was killed. A total of 51 wounds were found on his body, 18 of these were inflicted with sharp weapons. The nature of the weapons used shows the intent and diabolical nature of the crime. They fell to the level of being animals. Even after the victim died, they kept on the assault," he said.Calling it a "cold-blooded murder", Pandey added, "These people turned into butchers during the crime. There was not even a single cloth except underwear on the body of Sharma. These people should be kept behind bars, (and) given the maximum death sentence."Opposing the state's plea, Hussain's counsel, advocates Rajiv Mohan and Tara Narula, argued that no specific role had been attributed to their client and that six of the 11 accused had been acquitted in the case.Mohan submitted that the death penalty is warranted only in the "rarest of rare cases", adding that "the punishment of death cannot be determined merely on the basis of the injuries sustained. His (Hussain) conduct was good in jail during the custody."Referring to Hussain's acquittal under Section 120B (criminal conspiracy) of the erstwhile Indian Penal Code, the defence further argued, "Police themselves were unable to control the violent mob, and in such a situation, a single individual cannot be held responsible for the murder. He should be given a chance to reform."Hussain was earlier convicted of murder, kidnapping or abduction with intent to secretly and wrongfully confine a person, rioting and unlawful assembly, promoting enmity between groups, and disobedience of a public servant's order under erstwhile IPC.
Article Summary: Ib staffer murder case: prosecution seeks death sentence for tahir hussain, other convicts. Hussain, nazim, kasim, javed and anas were convicted on july 13. Special public prosecutor madhukar pandey argued that the murder was "exceptionally brutal"

Article Title: July 20 NEET protest: SC asks states to release student protesters under 18 with no criminal records
Article Text:
"Whosoever committed excesses, took law in their hands should be taken to task," SC observed.

ALSO READ |

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday directed Delhi and all state governments to release all arrested or detained protesters under the age of 18 with no criminal antecedents and ordered the police to preserve all digital evidence.The court also noted that a fair and independent probe into all allegations of "police excesses against protesting NEET students" was required. The top court's observations come as the opposition continues to protest the use of pellet guns against demonstrators marching towards Parliament on July 20."Whosoever committed excesses, took law in their hands should be taken to task", the court ovserved as per news agency PTI, adding: "Once there is violation of defined protocol, law must take care of it."The top court said a prima facie case had been made out for a transparent inquiry by a commission and added that the exercise should help frame a protocol for handling such situations in the future.The hearing also brought before the court allegations of police excesses from several states, including claims that a police officer in Bihar used an AK-47 against peaceful protesters.The Supreme Court also sought responses by Monday from states where incidents of violence were reported during the student protests.The apex court further directed the authorities to preserve digital records collected through CCTV cameras, facial recognition systems and drones. It ordered that such material, as well as the personal data of protesters, must not be placed in the public domain.Senior advocate Prashant Bhushan separately referred to a petition filed on behalf of protest volunteer Junaid Malik, alleging that he and his family were assaulted by the police.Taking note of the submissions, Chief Justice Surya Kant said the material placed before the court suggested there were allegations that warranted closer examination."If we start looking at individual facts… the most conservative language we can use is that there is, prima facie, a case of violence involved. That’s why we are hearing these matters."Appearing for the central government and the Delhi Police, solicitor general Tushar Mehta said the petitioners had accused the police of using excessive force during the protests and maintained that any wrongdoing by the police must be dealt with."If that is the case, they must be punished and action must be taken."At the same time, Mehta told the court that more than 250 police personnel had also sustained injuries during the protests."There is one truth, another truth, and then there is The truth, which this Court needs to examine."The chief justice observed that the allegations of attacks on police personnel also required investigation and sought clarity on who was responsible."For these attacks on police officials, the issue also needs to be addressed. Is it done by students or by…?"Responding to the query, Mehta said the authorities did not believe the students had attacked the police. He submitted that the violence may have been carried out by miscreants or "uninvited guests" who had infiltrated the protest.Justice Joymalya Bagchi also cautioned against attributing violence to an entire movement, observing, "There are always people discrediting a peaceful crowd."
Article Summary: "whosoever committed excesses, took law in their hands should be taken to task," sc observed. The top court's observations come as the opposition continues to protest the use of pellet guns against demonstrators marching towards parliament on july 20. The hearing also brought before the court allegations of police excesses from several states.

Article Title: 1 officer, 1 car: Government tightens rules for use of official vehicle for staff
Article Text:
Representative image

NEW DELHI: Government has tightened the rules governing the use of official vehicles by employees, stating an officer entitled to a govt staff car cannot be allotted more than one official vehicle, even when they hold additional charge of another ministry, department, public sector undertaking, or autonomous body.In addition, it has barred officers entitled from using vehicles belonging to PSUs and autonomous bodies, except when they are on official tour.In an official circular issued to all ministries and departments, the department of expenditure Monday, sought "strict compliance" to optimise vehicle utilisation and "prevent misuse of govt vehicles". It has asked all govt departments to keep unutilised vehicles in safe custody. The circular, was termed by officials as 'one officer, one official car'.The circular reinforces guidelines issued in Sept 2022, which specified that officers entitled can use official cars for personal travel (up to 500 km/month) by paying a fee of Rs 3,000 per month and giving up their standard monthly transport allowance.
Article Summary: An officer entitled to a govt staff car cannot be allotted more than one official vehicle. In addition, officers entitled from using vehicles belonging to psus and autonomous bodies, except when they are on official tour. The circular, was termed by officials as 'one officer, one official car'

Article Title: Delulu opposition thinks youth are with it, Rahul suffering from FOMO: NDA
Article Text:
File photo: Congress MP Rahul Gandhi and BJP MP Tejasvi Surya

NEW DELHI: BJP and its allies Tuesday lauded govt's engagement with protesting students, asserted the youth believe in PM Narendra Modi's ability to root out the menace of paper leaks and turned to Gen Z's lingo to mock leader of the opposition Rahul Gandhi as they mounted a sharp counterattack on the opposition in Lok Sabha."I will tell you in Gen Z language. Because of this issue (protest), opposition thinks the youth are with them. There is no bigger 'delulu' than it. Gen Z knows if any govt is working, then it is Modi govt," BJP MP Tejasvi Surya said, accusing rivals of spreading cynicism and anarchy, while Modi has used the crisis to launch root-and-branch reforms in the education system.Another party MP Anurag Thakur hit out at opposition parties for using students for their political gains and cited numerous incidents of paper leaks when they were in office in different states. When SP was in office in UP, the state service commission served the interest of one caste, and its chairperson Anil Yadav's appointment was struck down by HC, he said, amid noisy protest by SP members.Thakur's attack followed govt's robust defence from another party MP Bansuri Swaraj, who was the first speaker from the alliance, as she accused the opposition of "selective outrage" over paper leaks, saying such incidents frequently happened during the Congress-led UPA's term in office.Amid opposition's jibes, she said it was not about whataboutery but calling out the opposition. Targeting Congress, NDA members were prompt in sympathising with the concerns expressed by protesting students, asserting govt has heard them and offering suggestions to govt.Shiv Sena's Shrikant Shinde targeted Rahul over his protests, saying he sat on a dharna outside Modi's residence as he thought he was "MIA" (missing in action) and suffered from 'FOMO' (fear of missing out), but no student joined his demonstration.TDP's Lavu Sri Krishna Devarayalu suggested govt reform the burgeoning coaching system, suggesting it preyed on students' aspirations. Its market is around Rs 56,000 crore and will zoom to Rs 1 lakh crore in 6-7 years, he said, adding education should not be profit-driven, a point backed by Shinde too.Alleging that opposition sent anti-social elements to the student protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar who used filthy language and abuses for Modi, the Shiv Sena member said the engagement with protesters underscored govt's democratic commitment."We did not confine ourselves to condemnation but took up the task of cleaning the system. Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on moral grounds and not because of you (opposition)," he said, praising a series of measures taken by govt to reform the examination system.
Article Summary: Bjp and its allies lauded govt's engagement with protesting students. They asserted the youth believe in pm narendra modi's ability to root out the menace of paper leaks. They turned to gen z's lingo to mock leader of the opposition rahul gandhi.

Article Title: NEET protest: All SOPs followed, pellet gun use on protesters authorised, reveals CRPF review
Article Text:
File photo: July 20 NEET protest march

‘Police, RAF attacked with stones, iron rails’

NEW DELHI: All standard operating procedures (SOPs) and anti-riot drills were followed during the July 20 police action against anti-NEET leak protesters, which included the authorised use of "non-lethal" means like pellet gun, a CRPF post-event analysis has said.CRPF sources told TOI that upon carefully examining the response of its anti-riot unit, Rapid Action Force, it is evident that force gradient was followed, with pump action gun being used only after lower-grade measures like public announcements for crowd dispersal, tear gas and lathicharge failed to effectively control the mob. Around 3-5 protesters were injured by the metal pellets. Also, 47 RAF personnel were injured, with six sustaining head injuries.When contacted, CRPF DG G P Singh said the matter was "sub judice" and any findings or view of the force on RAF action would be placed before Supreme Court. RAF sources said the use of force on July 20 was authorised by Delhi Police, in line with the SOPs and the law.Sources claimed the mob had some motivated elements attacking personnel of Delhi Police and RAF with stones and, in some cases, even iron rails.As per BNSS, an executive magistrate may order use of civil force to disperse an unlawful assembly after carefully assessing the situation.In Delhi, this magisterial authority is vested with the Delhi Police commissioner, and delegated to junior commissioners till the level of the assistant commissioner of police. “RAF deployed at protest sites uses anti-riot gear only with authorisation; which in this case came from the DCP/ACP in charge of the protest site. Such authorisation is in writing and as per a format used at all sites of unlawful assembly; no order is given verbally,” said an officer.CRPF sources said pump action guns are an approved, “non-lethal” measure to control unlawful assemblies. “Their use, with the force gradient being followed and under authorisation by the competent officer, is as per the SOP,” said an officer.J&K high court had, in its 2016 ruling on a PIL challenging pellet use, said: “So long as there is violence by unruly mobs, use of force is inevitable. What kind of force has to be used at the relevant point of time or in a given situation has to be decided by the persons in charge of the place where the attack is happening. This court in writ jurisdiction, without any finding rendered by the competent forum/authority cannot decide whether the use of force in a particular incident is excessive or not. ”Supreme Court later dismissed the special leave petition against this order, stating, “The use of pellet guns, if at all done by any agency, has not only not been barred, but validated through these orders.”
Article Summary: All standard operating procedures (sops) and anti-riot drills were followed during the july 20 police action against anti-neet leak protesters. Crpf sources said force gradient was followed, with pump action gun being used only after lower-grade measures like public announcements for crowd dispersal, tear gas and lathicharge failed to control the mob.

Article Title: 'Uninformed, unacceptable': CJP claims SC order contradicts govt assurance; warns of protest
Article Text:
CJP gives it's statement to the government

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP ) has threatened to restart its nationwide agitation if the government fails to withdraw FIRs against student protesters, saying a Supreme Court interim order on the batch of PILs related to the protest "rings alarm bells across the country. "In an urgent statement posted on X, CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das said Direction No. 4 of the order is a "direct contradiction" to the government's solemn assurance of July 25 that FIRs would be withdrawn and protesters would not be targeted. The Direction permits governments to proceed with existing FIRs and carry out investigations."It was on the strength of that solemn assurance, and in complete good faith, that the Cockroach Janta Party called off its nationwide protest," Das said.The CJP spokesperson expressed apprehension that the government and BJP-ruled states may "weaponise" the order passed by the bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant to continue FIRs against individual protesters and subject them to harassment. "This was precisely our concern from day one: that courts could be used, directly or indirectly, to achieve political ends by targeting peaceful dissent," he said.Das also pointed to the fact that the interim order was not opposed by the government's lawyers, despite the Centre being fully aware that talks with the CJP had continued until late Monday night and that a "solemn agreement" had already been arrived at on July 25. "The court's uninformed order is therefore wholly unacceptable," he said."A solemn public assurance given to thousands of young students and protesters cannot be diluted, undermined, or rendered meaningless through subsequent legal developments, in a surreptitious manner. It only results in breach of public trust," Das added.He clarified that nothing in the interim order prevents the government or BJP/NDA-ruled states from withdrawing FIRs or deciding not to proceed against peaceful protesters, as done by Bihar and Assam governments. "The power to withdraw or not pursue such cases continues to rest with the executive. The court has not mandated that governments must definitely continue with the FIRs. That would be a deliberate misreading," he said.Das demanded that the government immediately place the terms of the July 25 assurance before the Supreme Court "so that there is complete transparency regarding the commitments already made to the youth of this country.""The youth of India entered into this understanding in good faith. That good faith must not be betrayed. Institutions of constitutional importance must never be politicised and weaponised to not honour the guarantees," he said.The CJP spokesperson said the deadline for the government to honour its guarantees expires on Tuesday. "We once again call upon it to fulfil every commitment it made: withdraw the FIRs, ensure that no protester is subjected to future punitive action, and honour both the letter and the spirit of the assurance that brought an end to the protest."He warned that if the guarantees are not honoured, the CJP will have "no option but to resume its nationwide protest." "A government that breaks its word cannot expect the youth to remain silent. If the guarantees are dishonoured, the streets of India will once again become the voice of its young," Das said.The CJP had called off its 36-day agitation at Jantar Mantar on July 25 after the government accepted its key demands, including the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
Article Summary: The cockroach janta party (cjp) has threatened to restart its nationwide agitation if the government fails to withdraw firs against student protesters. The cjp had called off its 36-day agitation at jantar mantar on july 25 after the government accepted its key demands. The deadline for the government to honour its guarantees expires on tuesday.

Article Title: Centre may table bill to make deepfakes, digital arrest separate offences
Article Text:
Digital arrest (representative image)

NEW DELHI: Government on Tuesday said it may introduce a bill in the ongoing session of Parliament making digital arrest and AI-generated deepfakes a distinct offence, after Supreme Court pointed out that existing penal laws do not define these offences.Solicitor General (SG) Tushar Mehta said the law will be aimed at categorising digital arrest and AI-generated deepfakes as specific offences with consequential punishments.During suo motu proceedings on the mechanism to curb the menace of digital arrest, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said SC has taken a harsh stand against those involved in digital arrest scams and denied them bail, but asked do penal laws define such offences?“You (govt) may need to formally define the case of digital arrest in penal laws,” the bench told attorney general R Venkataramani.“It (digital arrest) has elements of extortion, robbery and organised crime. Do you need to define this as a standalone offence with stringent consequences like freezing of assets of accused persons?” the bench asked attorney general R Venkataramani, who has been coordinating with a high-level inter-departmental committee constituted especially for dealing with the menace of digital arrest.Justice Bagchi said coming up with a law designed to deal with digital scams is a job that govt alone can do.“We now have deepfakes which can be used for misleading people or can be used for cheating and impersonation. Using our (exclusive) powers under Article 142 of the Constitution, we can neither define a crime nor create a new offence,” he said.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta told the bench that he has been consulted on this issue by govt and it is likely to introduce a relevant bill in the present session of Parliament. Venkataramani said because of a coordinated action facilitated by the inter-departmental committee, incidents of digital arrest have recorded a drastic fall. He said the panel is in the process of finalising a comprehensive report to identify gaps in the system and measures to plug them.Supreme Court after taking suo motu cognizance of spiralling incidents of digital arrest, especially targeting retired people and robbing them of their life’s savings, had tasked CBI to probe incidents being reported from across the country.Appearing for WhatsApp, senior advocate Kapil Sibal told SC that the social media platform is coordinating with govt to stop misuse of the platform for commission of crime.
Article Summary: Solicitor general tushar mehta said the law will be aimed at categorising digital arrest and ai-generated deepfakes as specific offences. Supreme court pointed out that existing penal laws do not define these offences. Justice bagchi said coming up with a law to deal with digital scams is a job that govt alone can do.

Article Title: Ahmedabad tragedy: Supreme Court accepts pilot dad's plea not to make Air India crash report public
Article Text:
SG Mehta said the government will submit the final report, as soon as it is finalised, to the SC in a sealed cover

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Tuesday accepted the request of the father of the pilot, who died in the Ahmedabad air crash last June, for not making public the final inquiry report, expected in Oct, and the Centre said that it will furnish the report in a sealed cover to the court.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta told a bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that govt respects the sentiments of the pilot's father and will submit the final report, as soon as it is finalised, to Supreme Court in a sealed cover. The SG, however, brushed aside objections to the ongoing inquiry into the crash of Air India's London flight that killed 260, all but one passenger and many on ground.Appearing for the NGO, advocate Prashant Bhushan attempted to punch holes in the inquiry, terming it to be biased because of absence of independent members in the probe team and said it did not follow the standard operating procedure for such inquiries. The solicitor general said the inquiry is being conducted following prescribed process scrupulously.Air Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) on July 14 had responded to the petition filed by the deceased pilot's father Pushkar Raj Sabharwal, and said, "In view of the nature, scale and complexity of the present accident, the AAIB has carefully assessed the timeline for completion of the investigation.In all probability, the investigation activities, subject to resolution of the pending external dependencies, are anticipated to be completed within six weeks. ""Thereafter, the draft final report, following completion of the analysis phase, is expected to be ready approximately in Oct 2026," it had said. "As per the treaty mandate, upon preparation of draft final report, the same has to be mandatorily shared with the Accredited Representatives of the State of Design and Manufacture, for comments, as required under the relevant rules of International Civil Aviation Organisation , which in the present case - the National Transportation Safety Board, USA. "
Article Summary: Court accepts request of father of pilot who died in ahmedabad air crash. Centre said that it will furnish the report in a sealed cover to the court. Air india's london flight that killed 260, all but one passenger and many on ground. Air accident investigation bureau (aaib) on july 14 had responded to the petition.

Article Title: NEET row: CBI chargesheets 13 in paper leak
Article Text:
File photo: NEET-UG 2026 leak probe

3 NTA subject experts and several middlemen among those named

NEW DELHI: Seventy-seven days after it filed an FIR and began a probe into the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak case, CBI Tuesday filed a chargesheet against 13 individuals arrested in the case. These include three NTA subject experts, in chemistry, biology and physics. Several middlemen who sourced and distributed these leaked questions have also been charged.The agency has cited 360 witnesses, 422 documents and 43 material objects to back its case, which concluded that persons responsible for setting the questions had leaked them, in connivance with their associates, including middlemen and coaching centre owners.The accused have been charged with offences of criminal conspiracy, cheating, criminal breach of trust, destruction of evidence and others under BNS, for the offence of criminal misconduct under Prevention of Corruption Act and for offences under Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024."Digital forensic analysis reports, handwriting expert opinions and academic experts' opinions regarding leaked questions were obtained.These reports confirmed the role of the accused in the circulation of leaked questions prior to the date of examination," CBI said in its final report. All 13 accused persons are in judicial custody. If the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill is passed, their trial is expected to be completed within three months. CBI had started an investigation on a complaint of the department of higher education on May 1, detailing irregularities and allegations of a paper leak in the NEET-UG 2026 examination."The probe team led by agency chief Praveen Sood acted swiftly to unearth the source of the leak within weeks of registration of the case. The channel from source of the leak to the beneficiary candidates was unearthed, leading to the identification of the chain," an officer said.After the filing of an FIR, Sood immediately formed multiple teams comprising 72 officers and personnel along with eight cyber forensic experts. "Searches were conducted at 92 locations in Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Haryana, Delhi and other states. These searches led to seizure of incriminating material like digital and communication devices, documents, etc," a CBI officer said.Forensic imaging and analysis of the incriminating material was undertaken. Intelligence agencies also gave crucial technical inputs. The first arrest in this case was made on May 13, within 24 hours of registration of the case. A dozen others were subsequently arrested from Pune and other places.The accused, arrested and now chargesheeted, include NTA subject experts Manisha Mandhare (biology), Pralhad Vithalrao Kulkarni (chemistry) and Manisha Sanjay Havaldar (physics), along with middlepersons and intermediaries Manisha Sanjay Waghmare, Dhananjay Nivrutti Lokhande, Shubham Madhukar Khairnar, Yash Yadav, Mangilal Biwal, Vikash Biwal, Dinesh Biwal and Dr Manoj Bhagwanrao Shirure.The chargesheet also names prominent coaching institute figures Shivraj Raghunath Motegoankar, owner of RCC Coaching Institute in Latur, and Tejas Harshadkumar Shah, physics faculty member and COO at APMA Coaching Institute in Pune.The money trail analysis has been conducted and several bank accounts, bank lockers and a demat account of the accused have been frozen. "Further investigation and forensic analysis is continuing in the case. CBI is committed to ensuring that those responsible for such offences face full legal consequences for their actions," the spokesperson added.With pending forensic reports expected in the coming days, CBI is likely to file a supplementary chargesheet in the case, the sources said.
Article Summary: Cbi files chargesheet against 13 individuals arrested in the neet-ug 2026 paper leak case. These include three nta subject experts, in chemistry, biology and physics. Several middlemen who sourced and distributed these leaked questions have also been charged.

Article Title: Congress, BJP spar over Pralhad Joshi's pick as education minister
Article Text:
BJP says the charge is baseless

NEW DELHI: Congress and BJP sparred over the choice of Union minister Pralhad Joshi being given the charge of the education ministry , with leader of the opposition Rahul Gandhi accusing him of defending rapists and BJP's chief spokesperson Anil Baluni hitting back by accusing Rahul of distorting facts for an individual's character assassination.Rahul alleged that Joshi had, in a TV interview a few years ago, justified the release of those convicted of the gang rape of Bilkis Bano during the 2002 Gujarat riots, and dubbed the Union minister a "filthy man".The charge, made after Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla had expunged remarks by Rahul's sister, Wayanad MP and Congress general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, drew a fierce response from Baluni, "This is unfortunate, deplorable and unacceptable."Accusing Rahul of making "misleading and factually incorrect" statements about Joshi's TV interview, the Pauri Garhwal MP said, "Joshi never tried to defend anybody. He was commenting on the process of remission and made no comment on the merits of the case."Speaking to reporters outside Parliament, Rahul said, "After all these young people protesting about the education system and so many girls protesting and being beaten and thrashed, BJP has given the charge of the ministry to a man who is a defender of rapists.There can be no filthier man than somebody who says rapists need protection. That is the education minister of India today."He added, "It is strange. It's a strange reaction from the Prime Minister. There are so many people in his cabinet. He could have chosen any one of them. But he chooses a person who protects rapists. It's quite amazing."Coming down hard on the Gandhi siblings, Baluni, head of BJP media cell, said the two should try to get their facts right and understand them. "They twist facts to suit what is convenient for them. They always make baseless charges to mislead people," he said.
Article Summary: Bjp says the charge is baseless and rahul gandhi is distorting facts for an individual's character assassination. Rahul alleged that joshi had, in a tv interview a few years ago, justified the release of those convicted of the gang rape of bilkis bano.

Article Title: 'Modiji clocked it': BJP MP's Gen Z-style praise for PM during anti-paper leak Bill debate
Article Text:
BJP MP's Gen Z-style praise for PM during anti-paper leak Bill debate

NEW DELHI: The Bharatiya Janata Party Lok Sabha member Bansuri Swaraj on Tuesday used a Gen Z term to praise the steps taken by Prime Minister Narendra Modi against the paper leak. She said that the PM had "clocked it" with the anti-paper leak Bill, a term used by the younger generation to recognize a fact.Speaking in favour of the Bill during the debate, she said, "Borrowing Gen Z's language, I would have to say that Modiji clocked it at providing this legislative solution"."I am standing in support of the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026. This is a transformative amendment. Its necessity is not only evident, but it is also the demand of the present time. Bringing this amendment is proof of the sensitivity of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his committed government. Speaker Sir, when a competitive examination is compromised, its impact is not limited to the candidate whose future is put at stake," she added.The government has proposed amendments to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act to ensure time-bound investigations, speedy trials and tougher penalties for paper leaks and organised exam fraud.Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced on Sunday the formation of a high-powered task force, headed by Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani, to overhaul India's examination system and make it more transparent, reliable and technology-driven.Addressing students through a video message, PM Modi said the Centre had already taken steps to curb exam malpractice by jailing those involved, setting up fast-track courts and proposing stricter legal provisions, but stressed that broader systemic reforms were now needed.He said the task force would recommend measures to strengthen the credibility of public examinations, with the government acting on its report at the earliest. The Nilekani-led panel will study the use of technology and suggest reforms to improve transparency, efficiency and trust in the conduct of public examinations.The move comes in the wake of recent controversies surrounding competitive examinations, including the NEET row, as the Centre seeks to restore confidence in the system.
Article Summary: Bjp mp bansuri swaraj uses gen z-style praise for pm during anti-paper leak bill debate. Pm narendra modi announced formation of high-powered task force to overhaul india's examination system. The move comes in the wake of recent controversies surrounding competitive examinations, including the neet row.

Article Title: PM Modi's message to key ministries: Be youthful, dynamic and adaptable
Article Text:
File photo: PM Modi

NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi on Tuesday told top officials of key economic ministries that govt must remain youthful and forward looking, a message that came days after he took to Instagram amid Gen Z-led protests against paper leaks."...a govt must always remain youthful, dynamic, forward-looking, continuously adapting to new challenges and opportunities with agility and innovation," PM was quoted as saying in a statement issued after his meet with secretaries and officials of ministries dealing with finance, commerce, industry and technology.He also called for the active participation of young entrepreneurs in key sectors, while asking officials to devise courses in consultation with the industry so that the workforce is equipped with skills required in emerging sectors.While education institutions have been producing a large number of engineers, professionals and graduates, often skill gap has emerged as a challenge for industry and govt's skilling initiative through the internship scheme has not had the desired impactso far.The other strong message was on addressing disinformation. "PM also emphasised the importance of proactive communication on strategic sectors where the country is undertaking major initiatives, to counter misinformation and unfounded fears surrounding such efforts," the statement said.He also underlined the need to keep citizens at the centre of every policy and decision. "Emphasising that reforms are not merely a fashionable term but a continuous necessity for effective governance, PM stressed the need to reform processes, improve work culture and strengthen institutional efficiency,"
Article Summary: Pm narendra modi told top officials of key economic ministries that govt must remain youthful and forward looking. Message came days after he took to instagram amid gen z-led protests against paper leaks. He also called for the active participation of young entrepreneurs in key sectors.

Article Title: After stalemate, government, opposition spar over paper leak law in Lok Sabha
Article Text:
File photo: Lok Sabha proceedings underway during the Monsoon Session of Parliament

Don’t view paper leaks through political lens, says Jitendra Singh

NEW DELHI: The week-long washout of Lok Sabha proceedings gave way to a fiery debate on Tuesday over the bill to make punitive measures more stringent and trial speedier in paper leak cases, as opposition members backed the students’ protests and criticised police’s alleged excesses against the protestors.Speakers from the BJP-led NDA brought up incidents of paper leaks during the UPA’s term and in states governed by opposition parties to emphasise that the menace had persisted irrespective of the party in office, and asserted that the country’s youth believed in PM Narendra Modi’s ability to usher in reforms to end it.Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra said Modi must take responsibility for the “injustice” with the youth, and he and home minister Amit Shah should answer as to who authorised the “use” of pellet guns on protestors in Delhi and an AK-47, which relates to an incident in Bihar with state police saying the gun was fired in the air in self-defence, in handling the agitation.Speakers from BJP and its allies acknowledged the concerns of students, and said the fact that govt engaged with them and had come out with a slew of measures underscored its democratic spirit. Students did not join Rahul Gandhi’s protest, some of them pointed out.Speaking on the Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill as the debate began a little after 2pm, Union minister Jitendra Singh said the “malaise” of paper leaks had affected state-level and national exams irrespective of the party in office and lauded the proposed law as a reaffirmation of govt’s commitment to safeguard students’ welfare.“Government’s intentions are honest and the amendment has been brought with an honest attitude. No member of any party should have any objection to it and if they have, then people will have objections to them,” he said.The minister of state in the PMO said govt had learnt from experience as any responsible govt should, emphasising the more stringent punishment proposed against individuals, organised gangs and entities involved in any paper leak, coupled with provisions for speedy justice.BJP MP Anurag Thakur said paper leak was no less a danger than terrorism and Maoism, as it targeted the youth first. “I want to tell the youth of the country that we will fully cure this disease of paper leaks because Modi govt has given us medicine for all diseases so far,” he said.Amid criticism of NTA, which organises several pan-India competitive exams, including NEET, Singh said back in 1992, a recommendation was first made to govt that there should be a common national testing agency.“Then, in 2010, during UPA govt, there was again a committee which suggested this. I do not know why this was not given due consideration. You must compliment PM Modi and this govt. It has finished an unfinished task which you should have accomplished,” he said.Citing recent paper leaks in Punjab and Karnataka, where AAP and Congress are in office, respectively, besides several other states where opposition parties have held office, Singh stressed that paper leaks should not be seen through a political lens.
Article Summary: Speakers from the bjp-led nda brought up incidents of paper leaks during the upa’s term and in states governed by opposition parties. Opposition members backed the students’ protests and criticised police's alleged excesses against the protestors. Union minister jitendra singh: paper leaks should not be seen through political lens.

Article Title: Gandhi siblings vs Pralhad Joshi: 'Defender of rapists' charge meets 'authenticate it' challenge
Article Text:
Pralhad Joshi; Priyanka Gandhi Vadra

NEW DELHI: Congress MPs Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of appointing as the new education minister a leader who had "expressed happiness over the release of those who raped a pregnant woman. "Union minister Pralhad Joshi has been given additional charge of the ministry of education following the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan on July 25 amid nationwide student protests over the NEET (UG) paper leak.Priyanka Gandhi Vadra was the first to target Joshi, making the remarks during the Lok Sabha debate on the Centre's proposed amendments to the anti-paper leak law."The prime minister appointed a new education minister, a person who expressed consent and even happiness over the release of those convicted of raping a pregnant woman," the Wayanad MP alleged, prompting Union minister Pralhad Joshi and parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju to intervene and demand that she substantiate the claim.An irate Joshi demanded that Priyanka Gandhi Vadra be expelled from the House and asked her to apologise for the remark.However, she hit back saying that has a video of the minister backing the convicted rapists."At a time when they are saying that they are bringing in women's rights, women's reservations and they are putting women in the forefront...It's a very wrong message...I am going to authenticate. There is a video of that time.I will submit everything with proper procedure," Priyanka Gandhi Vadra stated.Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi backed his sister and remarked that there cannot a "filthier" person than one who defends release of convicted rapists."Education minister of India - the BJP puts a man who is a defender of rapists. That is the most filthy type of man. There can be no flithier man than somebody who says that rapists need protection. That is the education minister of India today. It's a strange reaction from the PM, that there are so many people in his cabinet, he could have chosen anyone of them. But he chooses a person who protects rapists. Quite amazing!," Rahul Gandhi told reporters.The siblings appeared to be referring to the case of Bilkis Bano, who was gang-raped during the 2002 Gujarat riots. The 11 convicts were released in August 2022, triggering widespread outrage, before the Supreme Court quashed their release in January 2024.Speaking to a news channel in October 2022, Joshi had said the convicts' release was in accordance with the law.
Article Summary: Congress mps priyanka gandhi vadra and rahul gandhi target education minister pralhad joshi. Joshi has been given additional charge of the ministry of education following the resignation of dharmendra pradhan on july 25 amid nationwide student protests over the neet (ug) paper leak.

Article Title: Rajya Sabha adjourned as opposition seeks Shah statement on police action
Article Text:
File photo: Amit Shah

NEW DELHI: Rajya Sabha was adjourned for the day Tuesday amid repeated opposition protests demanding a statement from Union home minister Amit Shah over police action against demonstrators protesting the NEET-UG paper leak at Jantar Mantar.The House witnessed disruptions from the start of proceedings. It was first adjourned within minutes of assembling at 11am, after opposition MPs rose to raise the issue and demanded that Shah explain the police action against protesters.When RS reconvened at 2pm, deputy chairperson Harivansh attempted to take up govt's legislative business amid continued sloganeering.Union minister Jitan Ram Manjhi introduced Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill amid din. The proposed legislation was listed for introduction in the day's business. "There is a need to improve and modify the Act made in 2006," Manjhi said while introducing the bill.After its introduction, Harivansh sought to proceed to the next item - the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026 - which was listed for consideration and passage.However, Rajya Sabha could not take it up for discussion as opposition MPs continued their protest."So you don't want to run the House proceedings?" Harivansh asked the protesting MPs before adjourning the House till Wednesday.
Article Summary: Rajya sabha was adjourned for the day tuesday amid repeated opposition protests. Opposition mps demanded a statement from union home minister amit shah over police action against demonstrators protesting the neet-ug paper leak at jantar mantar. House witnessed disruptions from the start of proceedings.
